new_formative_fields.heading: Explain a timing experiment
new_formative_fields.purpose: fresh independent application before assistance; optional hint/model afterwards
new_formative_fields.prompt: In this model experiment, one small input produces a depolarization that stays below threshold. The same synapse is activated repeatedly, close together in time, and an action potential occurs. When the activations are far apart, it does not occur. Name the type of summation and explain all three observations. Would the successful trial require a taller action potential?

hint.heading: Optional hint: Ask what can overlap in time
hint.text: Make a first attempt before using this hint. Compare how much of an earlier postsynaptic effect remains when the next input arrives. Then keep the threshold decision separate from the height of the resulting spike.
hint.use: after a first independent attempt; assistance changes the evidence from independent to supported, but no runtime scoring/tracking is introduced

model.heading: Model and self-check
model.text: This is temporal summation. One input is insufficient. Closely spaced inputs arrive before earlier effects have faded, so the combined depolarization can reach threshold. Widely spaced inputs fade between activations and do not accumulate sufficiently. Reaching threshold triggers an ordinary all-or-none action potential; summation changes the likelihood of firing, not its height. Include timing and threshold in your explanation.

success_criteria: Identify temporal summation from repeated input at one synapse.
Explain fading versus overlap and threshold for all three model observations.

new_formative_fields.heading: Fresh application: distinguish input, output, and feedback
new_formative_fields.purpose: fresh independent application before assistance; optional hint/model afterwards
new_formative_fields.prompt: A student hears a cue, deliberately presses a small button, and notices that the finger overshoots it. The student adjusts the next attempt. Explain the sensory and motor roles, the CNS contributions to planning and coordination, and two cellular processes required along the pathway. Then predict what would change if ACh release at the finger muscle's neuromuscular junction were blocked while brain processing remained intact.

hint.heading: Optional hint: Trace one whole route, then zoom into two steps
hint.text: Make a first attempt before using this hint. Start with the sound and end with movement and adjustment. Insert cellular mechanisms where they do work. For the changed condition, locate the neuromuscular junction after the brain’s processing steps.
hint.use: after a first independent attempt; assistance changes the evidence from independent to supported, but no runtime scoring/tracking is introduced

model.heading: Model and self-check
model.text: Auditory input carries information toward the CNS. Connected brain regions interpret the cue and organize a voluntary response. Somatic motor output reaches finger skeletal muscles, while sensory feedback and cerebellar contributions help adjust accuracy. Axonal conduction requires threshold-dependent action potentials and regeneration; chemical synapses require release, diffusion, receptor binding, and clearance. If ACh release at the neuromuscular junction is blocked, the usual excitation of the muscle is reduced or absent even though a command was planned and could reach the terminal. Check for a connected pathway, distinct planning and coordination roles, two explained cellular mechanisms, and a prediction located at the affected junction.

success_criteria: Trace sound input, deliberate output and adjustment/feedback across CNS and effectors.
Explain at least two cellular processes, not just name parts.
Locate ACh release block at the NMJ despite intact brain processing.

new_formative_fields.heading: Optional application: compare two incomplete explanations
new_formative_fields.purpose: fresh independent application before assistance; optional hint/model afterwards
new_formative_fields.prompt: One claim says, “Addiction is only a matter of choosing badly.” Another says, “Once the brain changes, learning and environment no longer matter.” Explain what each leaves out, using one synaptic mechanism and one learning or context factor.

hint.heading: Optional hint: Connect a synaptic change with learning and context
hint.text: Make a first attempt before using this hint. Choose a communication step already taught, then connect it to a cue, repeated behaviour or an environmental influence. Check what each absolute claim leaves out.
hint.use: after a first independent attempt; assistance changes the evidence from independent to supported, but no runtime scoring/tracking is introduced

model.heading: Model and self-check
model.text: The first claim leaves out biological effects on signalling and circuits that influence motivation and behaviour; altered transmitter clearance is one possible mechanism. The second leaves out continuing learning, cue associations, environmental influences, and the capacity for change. For example, cues linked with repeated use can influence behaviour even after the immediate drug effect has ended. A strong response connects biology and learning without assuming a single cause or making a judgement about a person.

success_criteria: Identify what both moral-only and brain-change-only claims omit.
Connect a taught synaptic mechanism with learning/context without a deterministic or diagnostic conclusion.

concept_records.definition: receptor → sensory neuron → central nervous system → motor neuron → effector
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: The brain is the first structure in every nervous-system response.

concept_records.definition: sensory neurons carry information toward the CNS; motor neurons carry commands away
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: Sensory and motor neurons carry signals in the same direction.

concept_records.definition: rapid detection, integration and coordinated response
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: The nervous system only controls voluntary movement.

concept_records.definition: dendrites receive, the cell body maintains the cell, and the axon carries signals away
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: Dendrites normally carry impulses away from the cell body.

concept_records.definition: insulation around many axons that speeds conduction
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: Myelin is the electrical signal inside an axon.

concept_records.definition: the neuron region containing the nucleus and most organelles
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: The cell body is the gap between myelin segments.

concept_records.definition: a rapid pathway from receptor through sensory and integrating neurons to a motor neuron and effector
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: Every reflex requires a conscious decision before muscles respond.

concept_records.definition: a neuron within the CNS that connects and processes signals between neurons
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: Interneurons carry commands from the CNS directly to muscles.

concept_records.definition: a rapid, involuntary response that can reduce harm
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: A reflex never sends information to the brain.

concept_records.definition: a voltage difference across a resting neuron's membrane, with the inside negative relative to outside
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: A resting neuron has equal ion concentrations on both sides of its membrane.

concept_records.definition: active transport that moves three Na+ out for every two K+ moved in
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: The sodium–potassium pump opens only during depolarization and uses no energy.

concept_records.definition: the membrane allows some ions to cross more readily than others
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: Selective permeability means every ion crosses at the same rate.

concept_records.definition: a rapid, all-or-none reversal and restoration of membrane potential
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: A stronger stimulus creates a taller action potential in the same neuron.

concept_records.definition: the membrane potential becomes less negative as Na+ enters through voltage-gated channels
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: Depolarization is caused mainly by K+ leaving the neuron.

concept_records.definition: a recovery interval that limits immediate firing and supports one-way propagation
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: The refractory period makes the impulse travel backward and forward equally.

concept_records.definition: chemical communication from a presynaptic terminal across a cleft to receptors on a postsynaptic cell
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: Neurotransmitters normally travel down the axon as the action potential.

concept_records.definition: the combined effect of multiple excitatory and inhibitory postsynaptic inputs
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: Each synapse always acts alone and cannot combine with other inputs.

concept_records.definition: reuptake, enzymatic breakdown or diffusion ends a synaptic signal
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: Neurotransmitter must remain in the cleft permanently for signalling to stop.

concept_records.definition: a substance that activates a receptor or increases a neurotransmitter's effect
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: An agonist always blocks the receptor without activating it.

concept_records.definition: a substance that reduces signalling by blocking receptor activation
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: An antagonist necessarily increases neurotransmitter release.

concept_records.definition: slower transmitter removal that can prolong its effect in the synaptic cleft
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: Reuptake inhibition removes transmitter from the cleft faster.

concept_records.definition: somatic pathways control skeletal muscle; autonomic pathways regulate organs, glands and smooth or cardiac muscle
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: Autonomic control means every response is consciously chosen.

concept_records.definition: the autonomic division that generally supports activity and acute challenge
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: Sympathetic activity always slows the heart and promotes digestion.

concept_records.definition: the autonomic division that generally supports rest, digestion and recovery
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: Parasympathetic and sympathetic divisions produce identical effects in every organ.

concept_records.definition: bone, meninges and cerebrospinal fluid protect the brain and spinal cord
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: The meninges are neurons that carry motor signals.

concept_records.definition: gray matter contains many cell bodies and synapses; white matter contains many myelinated axons
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: White matter is white because it contains only dendrites and no axons.

concept_records.definition: a CNS pathway and integration centre linking brain, body and spinal reflexes
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: The spinal cord is part of the peripheral nervous system.

concept_records.definition: the largest brain region, supporting conscious perception, voluntary movement, language, memory and reasoning
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: The cerebrum's main role is directly controlling breathing rhythm.

concept_records.definition: a brain region that coordinates movement, balance and motor learning
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: The cerebellum initiates every conscious thought and language decision.

concept_records.definition: the region connecting brain and spinal cord that regulates vital automatic functions
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: The brain stem is responsible only for long-term memory storage.

concept_records.definition: CT uses X-rays for structural images; MRI uses magnetic fields and radio waves for detailed soft-tissue structure
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: MRI and EEG both directly record the same electrical signals from neurons.

concept_records.definition: electrodes at the scalp record patterns of electrical activity with high time resolution
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: EEG provides a sharply detailed three-dimensional image of deep brain anatomy.

concept_records.definition: each method provides particular evidence and has limits on structure, activity, timing and location
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: A colourful brain image proves the exact cause of a person's behaviour.

concept_records.definition: neural responses connect receptors, membrane events, synapses, CNS processing and effectors
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: Explaining a response requires naming only one neuron part.

concept_records.definition: a biological structure's features help explain what it can do
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: Naming a structure without a mechanism fully explains its function.

concept_records.definition: a correction identifies the inaccurate claim and replaces it with a mechanism supported by evidence
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: An error correction only says that a statement is wrong.

concept_records.definition: a chapter concept can support a cautious explanation without requiring personal disclosure or outside research
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: A personal story is required evidence for every biological explanation.

concept_records.definition: a model simplifies reality and must be interpreted within its stated boundaries
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: A diagram that omits detail is automatically useless.

concept_records.definition: check mechanism, evidence quality, alternatives and limits before accepting a claim
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: A higher price is biological evidence that a treatment works.

concept_records.definition: chapter mechanisms can help explain technologies and health decisions without grading opinions
concept_records.misconception_is_intentionally_false: An opinion becomes scientific evidence when it is stated confidently.
